ios.breadcrumbs: Use NavigationStack. Its back button and title carry the path.
ios.error-boundary: SwiftUI has no render errors to catch. Model failures as state and show StanceErrorState.
ios.floating-action-button: Put the primary action in the toolbar or a bottom bar, as iOS apps do.
ios.hover-card: Use .popover on iPad and a sheet on iPhone.
ios.tooltip: Use .help for pointer and the system popover for touch.
ios.icon-gallery: Not needed on device. Browse icons on the website.
ios.kbd: Use .keyboardShortcut so the system shows shortcuts in menus.
ios.link: Use Link, styled by the theme tint.
ios.menubar: Use the app's Commands, shown in the iPad menu bar.
ios.skip-link: VoiceOver rotor and headings cover this. Mark headings with .accessibilityAddTraits(.isHeader).
ios.virtualized-list: List and LazyVStack are already lazy.

android.breadcrumbs: Use the top app bar's up navigation and title.
android.caption: Use Text with the Stance caption style from the theme.
android.container: Use StanceScaffold with window size classes.
android.error-boundary: Compose has no render errors to catch. Model failures as state and show StanceErrorState.
android.heading: Use Text with a Stance heading style and Modifier.semantics { heading() }.
android.text: Use Text with Stance type styles from the theme.
android.hover-card: Use StancePopover. Hover only applies with a mouse.
android.icon-gallery: Not needed on device. Browse icons on the website.
android.image: Use Image and your image loader.
android.kbd: Use keyboard shortcuts in the system shortcut helper.
android.menubar: Use the top app bar's actions and overflow menu.
android.resizable-panel: Use the list detail scaffold from Material 3 adaptive.
android.scroll-area: Use Modifier.verticalScroll or a lazy list.
android.skip-link: TalkBack headings cover this. Mark headings with semantics { heading() }.
